name: split-button
title: Split button
purpose: A main action joined to a menu button that holds other ways to do the same thing.
whenToUse: When one action is right most of the time and two or more close alternatives are needed now and then, such as Start task and Start on a new branch.
When the alternatives are variations of the main action, so the reader would look for them beside it.
whenNotToUse: For actions that are not variations of one another. Use buttons, or a menu behind a button that names what they act on.
For a single alternative. Show it as a second button.
To choose a value that stays chosen. Use a select or a segmented control.
For an option that is on or off. Use a toggle button.

variants.name: secondary
variants.use: The default. Both halves are plain buttons.

variants.name: primary
variants.use: The main action also carries ds-button--primary when it is the one main action of the view. The menu button stays a plain button, so the pair never shows two accent fills.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: As tall as a control, 40px by default and 44px on a coarse pointer. The menu button is a square of that height.

accessibility: Use a div with ds-split-button, role="group" and an aria-label that names the main action. It holds the main action, then the menu button, then the menu, in that order.
The main action is a button with ds-button and ds-split-button__action. Its label is a verb and what it acts on. Pressing it never opens the menu.

The menu button is a button with ds-button and ds-split-button__toggle, popovertarget set to the menu's id and aria-haspopup="menu". It holds the chevron icon with aria-hidden="true" and its own name in a ds-visually-hidden span, such as More ways to start the task. The name is never the main action's label again.

The menu is the menu component, copied from its examples, with the same name as the menu button in its aria-label. Its items are other ways to do the main action. The main action itself is not repeated in it.
At most the main action is primary. Two primary halves fail the one-primary-action rule.

Tab reaches the main action and then the menu button. Enter and Space activate each. The browser opens and closes the menu, closes it on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the menu button. The keys inside the menu are the menu component's: wrap the ds-split-button in the ds-menu element of behaviors/menu.js, or handle them in the app, and focus moves to the first item when the menu opens, the arrow keys move it, and Tab closes the menu.
When the action is unavailable, set disabled on both halves. While the main action runs, set aria-busy="true" on it, change its label to say what is happening, and set disabled on the menu button.
The component needs no script of its own beyond the menu's.
